$ai_tools.name: list_active_listings

was just marked inactive will not appear. Takes no arguments

$ai_tools.description:
Searches recently closed and active comparable sales in the
agent's market area using a free-text query, for example
"3 bed under 500k in Maple Heights" or "closed sales on Birch
Street last 90 days". The search understands street names,
neighborhoods, price ranges written in plain English, bedroom
and bathroom counts, and property type, and returns each match

the agent can build a comparable market analysis without

listings; use list_active_listings for those. Results are
limited to the last three years of closed data plus everything
currently active, and a query that is too broad, such as a bare

recent matches rather than every record, so it is worth
narrowing the query with a price range or property type when
the agent needs a tighter comparable set.

the results toward documents about that property; otherwise the
search ranks across the whole knowledge base. This is the tool
the agent reaches for first when a client asks a question about
a property that is more detailed than price and square footage,
since the answer is usually sitting in a document rather than in
structured data. Returns the top matching passages with the
source document id, so a follow-up call to fetch_5QqGqw1K can pull
the full document if the excerpt is not enough context to answer

$ai_tools.name: create_followup_task
$ai_tools.description:
Creates a follow-up task tied to a document, such as a
reminder to call a lead back or to chase a signed disclosure.
document_id anchors the task to whatever it is about, most often
a contact note or a listing page. due_date_ts is a Unix
timestamp in seconds for when the task is due, priority is a
small integer where a lower number means more urgent, and

way to mark a task as skipped or cancelled other than deleting

integrations that read tasks back out, and recurrence_rule
follows the same short recurrence syntax used elsewhere in the
app, such as "weekly" or "monthly".

$ai_tools.name: reschedule_followup_task
$ai_tools.description:
Moves an existing follow-up task to a new due time rather
than creating a new one. task_id identifies which task to move,

same day the task was already due, and label lets the reason for
the move be recorded alongside the change, such as "client asked
to push to the afternoon". Set is_recurring to true if this move
should also apply to every future occurrence of a recurring
task rather than just the next one; the default only moves the
single upcoming occurrence and leaves the rest of the recurrence
untouched.

$ai_tools.name: add_checklist_item
$ai_tools.description:
Adds a new item to an existing checklist, such as a moving

identifies which checklist to add to and label is the text of

Logs feedback and details from a showing or open house

is already there. Use it to log a new update without touching
earlier wording.

$ai_tools.name: get_daily_briefing
$ai_tools.description:
Builds the morning briefing for the agent: today's showings
and open houses pulled from the calendar, any tasks due today
or overdue, flagged notes that still need review, and unread
follow-up reminders for leads that have gone quiet. This is the
same content shown on the app's home screen, so prefer this
tool over combining list_open_houses, get_daily_task_summary,
and list_active_listings separately when the user just asks
what is on for today. Takes no arguments.

$ai_tools.name: browse_i7ALoQrkwaUr
$ai_tools.description:
Lists every saved note in the current workspace, most
recently updated first, including its id, name, and a short
preview of the content. Does not return the full body of long
notes; call fetch_5QqGqw1K with a note's id for that. Archived
notes are excluded from the results.

$ai_tools.name: enrich_contact_profile
$ai_tools.description:
Looks up a contact's public LinkedIn profile and pulls their
current job title, employer, and location into the contact
record, which helps when qualifying a lead before a first call.
The lookup only reads public profile data; it cannot see
connections, posts, or anything behind a login wall. Results
are cached per contact for thirty days unless refresh is set,
so repeated calls for the same contact are cheap.

network_uf5tQu5n.description: The public LinkedIn profile URL or handle to look up.

refresh.description:
Whether to force a fresh lookup instead of using the last
cached LinkedIn snapshot for this contact, which otherwise
refreshes automatically every thirty days.

$ai_tools.name: list_recent_leads
$ai_tools.description:
Lists the agent's most recently added leads, newest first,
with their name, stage, and last contact date. Useful for a
quick check of who has come in without opening the full CRM
view. Pair with update_contact_record to move a lead forward
after reviewing this list.

category.description: Restrict the results to leads in this category, if given.

limit.description: Maximum number of leads to return.

$ai_tools.name: fetch_5QqGqw1K
$ai_tools.description:
Fetches the full content of a single saved document by id,
including every section and its current text. Use this before
change_TJXB19DD so the old_text argument matches exactly, and
before add_document_paragraph to confirm which section name to
target. Returns an error if the document has been deleted or
archived.

document_id.description: The unique identifier of the document.

$ai_tools.name: get_document_change_log
$ai_tools.description:
Returns the change history for a document: who or what made
each edit, a short description of the change, and a timestamp.
Use this to see whether a listing description was recently
updated before assuming it is stale, or to explain to the agent
why the wording changed since they last looked. Entries older
than ninety days are not kept.

document_id.description: The unique identifier of the document.

$ai_tools.name: list_document_comments
$ai_tools.description:
Lists comments left on a document by the agent or a
collaborator, newest first, with cursor-based pagination for
documents that have a long comment thread. Comments are plain
text notes attached to the document as a whole, not to a
specific section or line.

cursor_token.description: Continuation token returned by an earlier call, if any.

page_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to return per page.

$ai_tools.name: restore_document_version
$ai_tools.description:
Restores a document to an earlier saved version, overwriting
the current content in every section. Use list_document_versions
first to find the version number to restore, since this call
cannot be undone once the newer content has been overwritten.

version.description: The version number to restore, from the version list.

$ai_tools.name: list_document_versions
$ai_tools.description:
Lists every saved version of a document with its version
number, the time it was saved, and a one-line summary of what
changed. Listing descriptions typically go through several
revisions before a property goes live, and this is the only way
to see that history or to find a version number to pass to
restore_document_version.

$ai_tools.name: list_active_listings
$ai_tools.description:
Lists every listing currently marked active for the agent,
with its address, list price, days on market, and status. This
is the agent's own book of business, not a search of the wider
market: use search_property_records or search_web_listings
instead when the question is about comparable properties the
agent does not represent. The results here always reflect the
latest status set through set_listing_status, so a listing that
was just marked inactive will not appear. Takes no arguments
and returns every active listing regardless of how many there
are, so it can be a long list for a busy agent.

$ai_tools.name: search_comparables
$ai_tools.description:
Searches recently closed and active comparable sales in the
agent's market area using a free-text query, for example
"3 bed under 500k in Maple Heights" or "closed sales on Birch
Street last 90 days". The search understands street names,
neighborhoods, price ranges written in plain English, bedroom
and bathroom counts, and property type, and returns each match
with its close price, close date, and price per square foot so
the agent can build a comparable market analysis without
leaving the chat. It does not search the agent's own active
listings; use list_active_listings for those. Results are
limited to the last three years of closed data plus everything
currently active, and a query that is too broad, such as a bare
city name with no other filter, returns only the twenty most
recent matches rather than every record, so it is worth
narrowing the query with a price range or property type when
the agent needs a tighter comparable set.

$ai_tools.name: search_property_records
$ai_tools.description:
Runs a semantic search over the agent's full knowledge base
of property records: listing sheets, inspection reports,
disclosure documents, and past comparable market analyses that
have been saved into the workspace. Unlike search_comparables,
which only covers sale prices, this searches the actual document
text, so a query like "radon mitigation systems installed in the
last two years" or "listings with a shared driveway easement"
will match on details buried inside inspection reports and
disclosures rather than just structured sale data. Pass
listing_context with a specific address or MLS number to bias
the results toward documents about that property; otherwise the
search ranks across the whole knowledge base. This is the tool
the agent reaches for first when a client asks a question about
a property that is more detailed than price and square footage,
since the answer is usually sitting in a document rather than in
structured data. Returns the top matching passages with the
source document id, so a follow-up call to fetch_5QqGqw1K can pull
the full document if the excerpt is not enough context to answer
confidently.

listing_context.description:
An address or MLS number to bias the search toward,
if the question is about a specific property.

$ai_tools.name: search_contact_history
$ai_tools.description:
Searches free-text notes, call logs, and past messages
attached to the agent's contacts for a matching phrase, such as
"asked about waterfront" or "wants a fast close". This searches
across every contact rather than one record, which makes it
useful for finding every lead who mentioned a particular
requirement without paging through the CRM one contact at a
time. Returns each match with the contact's name and id so a
follow-up call to update_contact_record can act on it directly.
Does not search email threads outside the CRM.

$ai_tools.name: search_web_listings
$ai_tools.description:
Searches public listing sites for homes matching a query,
for example "3 bedroom condos in Riverside under 400k". This
looks outside the agent's own book of business at what is
currently on the open market, which is useful when a buyer asks
about competing inventory the agent does not represent. Results
may lag the live market by a few hours.

query.description:
The search query, for example a neighborhood, price range,
and bedroom count written as plain text.

$ai_tools.name: set_listing_status
$ai_tools.description:
Marks a listing as active or inactive on the market. Setting
active to false pulls the listing out of list_active_listings
and out of the public-facing site feed, but keeps its documents
and history intact for later reference. Use this when a listing
goes under contract, is temporarily withdrawn, or closes, rather
than deleting anything. This does not cancel any scheduled
showings or open houses tied to the listing; cancel those
separately if the property is coming off the market.

active.description: Whether the listing should be marked active on the market.

$ai_tools.name: edit_page_section
$ai_tools.description: Edits or inserts content into a page section.

section.description:
The name of the section to edit or create, such as
"Overview" or "Showing Notes".

after.description: The name of an existing section to insert this one after.

block_anchor.description: Id of a specific block to anchor the edit to, if any.

replace_mode.description:
Whether to replace the section's content instead of
appending to what is already there.

attachments.description:
Optional list of attachment objects to include with the
section, such as a photo or a floor plan file. Each object
needs at minimum a url and a caption; a missing caption is
allowed but the attachment will render without one in the final
page. This is separate from create_attachment, which saves a
standalone resource rather than embedding it directly into a
page section.

formatting_options.description:
Optional formatting hints such as heading level or
whether the section should render as a bulleted list.

$ai_tools.name: run_workspace_automation
$ai_tools.description: Runs a named workspace automation with optional arguments.

opts.description: Extra key-value arguments the automation needs, if any.

$ai_tools.name: update_contact_record
$ai_tools.description:
Updates one or more fields on an existing contact record.
Only the fields that are passed are changed; anything left out
keeps its current value. Use search_contact_history first if
you only have a name or a partial phrase to go on rather than a
contact id.

name.description: The contact's full name, if it is changing.

relationship_stage.description: Where the contact sits in the pipeline.

lead_source.description: Where this contact originally came from.

$ai_tools.name: change_LkbRMHYwQP5
$ai_tools.description:
Adds, removes, or renames a calendar event such as a
showing, an open house, or a closing appointment. When action
is "add", title and start are required and end defaults to one
hour after start if it is left out. When action is "rename", only
title changes and every other field is ignored even if it is
passed. When action is "remove", only calendar_event_id is used
and all other fields are ignored. Setting reminder_minutes adds
a notification that many minutes before the event starts; leave
it unset to use the agent's default reminder time. attendees
takes a list of email addresses and sends each of them a
calendar invite once the event is saved, so double check the
list before adding an event with action "add".

action.description: Whether to add, remove, or rename.

start.description: Start time in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

end.description: End time in ISO 8601 format; defaults to start plus one hour.

attendees.description: Email addresses to invite to the event.

meeting_link.description: A video call link to attach to the event, if any.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event with no start time.

$ai_tools.name: change_FihCwp7CUFy
$ai_tools.description:
Runs a bulk update across every listing matching the given
filters, for example marking every listing in a neighborhood as
price-reduced, or tagging a set of listing_ids with an amenity
that was missed when they were first entered. Leaving every
filter empty matches every active listing, so at least one
filter should usually be set before calling this with a write
like price_reduced_only.

listing_ids.description: Only update listings with one of these ids, if given.

property_types.description: Only match listings of these property types.

amenities.description: Only match listings with these amenities.

price_reduced_only.description: Only match a recent price drop.

listing_agent_email.description:
Only match listings whose agent-of-record matches this
email; leave unset to include listings for every agent on the
team, not just the caller.

custom_metadata_filters.description:
Arbitrary key-value filters to match against custom fields
set on a listing, such as a virtual tour vendor or a staging
company. Every key given must match exactly; there is no partial
or case-insensitive matching on these values. Leave this unset
unless the agent has actually set custom fields on the listings
being targeted, since an unmatched key filters out every result
rather than being ignored.

sort_by.description: Field to sort the matched listings by.

region.description: Only match listings in this region.

location.description: Only match this event's location field.

include_archived_listings.description: Whether to include archived listings in the match.

view_mode.description: How the matched listings should be sorted for display.

$ai_tools.name: compare_listing_snapshots
$ai_tools.description:
Compares two saved sets of listing snapshots and returns
what changed between them: price drops, status changes, and new
or removed listings. Useful for a weekly market-watch summary.

current_listing_snapshots.description:
The newer set of listing snapshot objects to compare,
usually pulled from search_web_listings or
search_property_records.

previous_listing_snapshots.description:
The older set of listing snapshot objects to compare
against, from an earlier run of the same search.

$ai_tools.name: archive_workspace_items
$ai_tools.description:
Archives one or more notes, tasks, or documents by id,
removing them from their normal list views without permanently
deleting them. Archived items can still be found through search
tools but no longer show up in browse_i7ALoQrkwaUr or
get_daily_briefing.

item_ids.description:
The ids of the items to archive. Mixed types are allowed
in the same call, for example archiving a note and a task
together, as long as every id belongs to one of the supported
item kinds.

$ai_tools.name: create_attachment
$ai_tools.description:
Saves a standalone attachment, such as a photo, a floor
plan, or a reference link, so it can be pointed to from a note
or a listing without re-uploading it each time. kind must be
url, image_upload, or plain_text and controls how content is
interpreted: for url it is the link itself, for image_upload it
is the already-uploaded image reference, and for plain_text it
is the literal text to save. Pass note_id to associate the new
attachment with an existing note; otherwise it is saved
unattached and can be linked in later through edit_page_section.

kind.description:
What kind of content this attachment holds. url expects a
link, image_upload expects an already-uploaded image reference,
and plain_text expects literal text saved as the attachment's
content.

content.description:
The url, image reference, or plain text, depending on which
kind was given for this attachment.

note_id.description: An existing note to attach this to, if any.

$ai_tools.name: broadcast_update
$ai_tools.description:
Posts a short update to the office activity feed, such as
"just listed 12 Birch Street" or "open house moved to Sunday".
Every agent on the team can see the feed from their own app, so
this is meant for things worth a quick heads-up rather than
private client details. Set notify_all_agents to also push a
notification instead of only adding the update to the feed.

$ai_tools.name: pin_workspace_note
$ai_tools.description:
Pins or unpins a note so it stays at the top of
browse_i7ALoQrkwaUr regardless of when it was last updated. Useful
for a note that needs to stay visible for the whole time a
listing is live, such as seller instructions or lockbox codes,
rather than getting buried under newer notes.

note_id.description: The id of the note to pin or unpin.

pinned.description: Whether the note is now pinned.

$ai_tools.name: delete_saved_note
$ai_tools.description:
Permanently deletes a saved note by id. Unlike
archive_workspace_items this cannot be undone, so consider
archiving instead unless the note was created by mistake or is
no longer needed for any reason.

note_id.description:
The id of the note to delete. This action is permanent
and cannot be undone.

$ai_tools.name: update_note_details
$ai_tools.description:
Updates the metadata on an existing note without touching
its content, such as renaming it, moving it into a different
folder, or sharing it with another agent. To change the note's
actual text, use change_TJXB19DD or add_document_paragraph on the
note's id instead. Fields left out of the call keep their
current value.

note_id.description:
The id of the note to update. Fields left out of the call
keep their current value.

title.description: New title for the note, if it is changing.

folder_id.description:
Move the note into this folder; pass null to remove it
from any folder.

reminder_date.description: A date to resurface this note.

is_shared.description: Whether other agents can view this note.

shared_with.description: Specific agent ids to share the note with, if is_shared.

$ai_tools.name: create_page
$ai_tools.description:
Creates a new blank page in the workspace with the given
title and returns its id. A page is a longer-form document made
up of named sections, meant for things like a full listing
package, a buyer presentation, or a closing checklist, rather
than the quick single-body notes made by create_workspace_note.
After creating a page, use edit_page_section to add its first
section, since a brand-new page starts out with no sections at
all and cannot be shared with a client until at least one
section has content. There is no limit on how many sections a
page can hold, but very long pages take noticeably longer to
load in the mobile app, so splitting a large closing package
into a few pages tends to work better than one page with dozens
of sections.

title.description:
The title for the new page. This is shown in every list
view and cannot be left blank, though it can be changed later
with update_note_details.

$ai_tools.name: save_quick_highlight
$ai_tools.description:
Saves a short quoted snippet with a label attached, for
quickly capturing something a client said on a call without
writing a full note. For example, saving the text "wants to be
in before the school year starts" with the label "timeline" so
it surfaces later when reviewing that client's file. These show
up alongside a contact's notes but stay separate from full note
content so they are quick to scan later, and a client's saved
highlights are shown together the next time their file is
opened, in the order they were originally captured.

text.description:
The exact text to save, usually a short quote taken
from a call or a message rather than a paraphrase of
what the client actually said, so the wording matches
exactly what comes up later when reviewing the file.

label.description:
A short label to group this highlight with others like
it, such as "timeline", "budget", or "must_have".

$ai_tools.name: get_conversation_thread
$ai_tools.description:
Fetches every message in a saved conversation thread by
id, in order, along with who sent each one. Threads are used to
keep a record of a back-and-forth with a client or another agent
outside of this chat, for example a text exchange forwarded in
for safekeeping. This does not include messages from this
assistant's own conversation with the agent, only threads that
were explicitly saved into the workspace.

$ai_tools.name: create_followup_task
$ai_tools.description:
Creates a follow-up task tied to a document, such as a
reminder to call a lead back or to chase a signed disclosure.
document_id anchors the task to whatever it is about, most often
a contact note or a listing page. due_date_ts is a Unix
timestamp in seconds for when the task is due, priority is a
small integer where a lower number means more urgent, and
assigned_agent is the id of whoever should see it on their task
list, which does not have to be the caller. status defaults to
active and can otherwise only be set to completed; there is no
way to mark a task as skipped or cancelled other than deleting
it outright. metadata accepts arbitrary extra fields for
integrations that read tasks back out, and recurrence_rule
follows the same short recurrence syntax used elsewhere in the
app, such as "weekly" or "monthly".

$ai_tools.name: reschedule_followup_task
$ai_tools.description:
Moves an existing follow-up task to a new due time rather
than creating a new one. task_id identifies which task to move,
hour is the new due hour in the agent's local timezone on the
same day the task was already due, and label lets the reason for
the move be recorded alongside the change, such as "client asked
to push to the afternoon". Set is_recurring to true if this move
should also apply to every future occurrence of a recurring
task rather than just the next one; the default only moves the
single upcoming occurrence and leaves the rest of the recurrence
untouched.

$ai_tools.name: add_checklist_item
$ai_tools.description:
Adds a new item to an existing checklist, such as a moving
checklist shared with a buyer or an open-house prep list. list_id
identifies which checklist to add to and label is the text of
the new item; both are required. Set is_recurring to true for an
item that should reappear automatically on every future use of
the same checklist template rather than only this one instance,
which is useful for a standing prep step like "turn on all the
lights" that applies to every open house rather than just the
next one.

$ai_tools.name: search_by_map_bounds
$ai_tools.description:
Searches active listings and comparable sales within a
rectangular map area defined by four coordinates, for drawing a
result set from a map view rather than a text query. All four
corners are required together; passing only some of them returns
an error rather than falling back to a default area. This is
meant to back a map-based search UI and behaves like a narrower,
coordinate-based version of search_comparables rather than a
replacement for it.

$ai_tools.name: log_showing_details
$ai_tools.description:
Logs feedback and details from a showing or open house
after the fact, attached to the calendar event_id it belongs to.
note is a free-text summary of how it went, response captures
the buyer or agent's reaction if one was given, venue records
where it actually took place if that differed from the calendar
listing, cost logs any expense tied to the event such as staging
or printed flyers, parking notes anything worth flagging for the
next visitor such as a blocked driveway, and agenda records what
was planned to be covered, which is useful when comparing what
was meant to happen against what response says actually
happened. Only event_id is required; every other field can be
filled in over several calls as details come in rather than all
at once.

$ai_tools.name: list_open_houses
$ai_tools.description:
Lists every open house on the calendar from today onward,
with its address, start and end time, and how many people have
responded to the associated poll if one was created with
create_showing_poll. Past open houses are not included; use
get_document_change_log or search_comparables for historical
sale data instead. Takes no arguments and always covers every
upcoming open house regardless of listing.

$ai_tools.name: create_showing_poll
$ai_tools.description:
Creates a poll to send to a client for picking a showing
time, with a topic and a list of time-slot options for them to
choose from. Once created, the poll can be shared with the
client outside of this chat, and get_poll_results reads back
whichever options they picked. topic is a short label such as
"12 Birch Street second showing" rather than a full question,
and options should be phrased as plain time slots like "Saturday
10am" or "Sunday 2pm" so they read cleanly wherever the poll is
sent. There is no limit on the number of options, but polls with
more than about six tend to get lower response rates in
practice, so it is usually worth narrowing to the times that
actually work before creating the poll.

$ai_tools.name: end_poll
$ai_tools.description:
Closes an open showing-time poll so no further responses
can be submitted. The poll's results remain available through
get_poll_results after it is closed, and closing it does not
notify anyone who has not yet responded, so it is worth checking
get_poll_results first if some invitees have gone quiet.

$ai_tools.name: get_poll_results
$ai_tools.description:
Returns every response submitted so far to a showing-time
poll, including which option each respondent picked. Works on
both open and closed polls.

$ai_tools.name: delete_poll_response
$ai_tools.description:
Deletes a single response from a showing-time poll, for
example after a client changes their mind on the phone instead
of updating the poll themselves. This removes only that one
response; the poll itself stays open and other respondents'
answers are untouched.
